text_plugin_synopsis: Batch renames files and folders with search and replace, regular expressions, counters and date variables

p_build_intro: This section targets developers who want to build the plugin from source.
p_introduction_what: The Batch Rename plugin adds batch renaming to AutoJs6, modeled on [PowerRename]({{ powerrename_url }}) from PowerToys: rename many files and folders at once with search and replace, regular expressions, counters, date and random variables, preview every result before anything changes, and undo afterwards.
p_introduction_how: The plugin is a separately installed APK without a launcher icon. It has two entry points: "Batch rename" in the file manager's multi-select toolbar, folder menu and rename dialog, and `files.batchRename` in scripts. The plugin only computes the new names; AutoJs6 performs the renames, the conflict checks and the undo records, so the plugin needs no storage permission.
p_status_note: This is a development preview: AutoJs6 recognizes the plugin, but the rename screen, the file manager entries and the script API are not delivered yet. The sections below describe the design goals of 1.0.0; see the roadmap for progress.
features: Search and replace: plain text or regular expressions, all matches or only the first, case sensitive or not, applied to the file name, the extension or the whole name.
Variables: counters (`${start=1;increment=1;padding=3}`), date variables from the modification time (`$YYYY`, `$MM`, `$DD` and more) and random strings, written as in PowerRename.

Text cleanup: case conversion, Unicode normalization, full-width to half-width conversion, illegal character cleanup, trimming of leading and trailing spaces and dots, and numbering that continues existing sequences.

Preview first: every item shows its old and new name, single items can be excluded, and conflicts and invalid names are marked; a conflict can reject the batch, skip the item, add a number or overwrite.
Undo: AutoJs6 keeps the last 20 rename batches; both the file manager and scripts can undo them after checking that the files have not changed again.
usage_steps: Update AutoJs6 to build {{ required_host_version_code }} ({{ required_host_version_name }}) or later.
Install Batch Rename from the AutoJs6 Plugin Center, or download the APK from [Releases]({{ repo_url }}/releases), then authorize and enable it in the Plugin Center.
Long-press in the file manager to select items and tap "Batch rename", or call `files.batchRename` in a script.
p_usage_note: The plugin ships a single universal APK for Android {{ min_android_version }} (API {{ android_min_sdk }}) and later. It does not add a launcher icon.
p_variables_intro: The replacement text can contain the following variables
td_variable_counter: Counter with start value, step and zero padding; it only advances for items that are renamed
td_variable_date: Year, month, day, hour, minute, second and millisecond of the modification time, or of the current time
td_variable_random: Random alphanumeric, letter or digit strings and UUIDs
td_variable_regex: Regular expression groups and the whole match, as in JavaScript's `String.prototype.replace`
p_script_api_intro: Scripts use the same engine through `files.batchRename` (1.0.0 design draft; the released documentation is authoritative)
api_points: `files.batchRename.plan(paths, options)` computes without renaming and returns a result per item; set `items[i].excluded` and pass the plan to `apply`.
`files.batchRename(paths, options)` renames in one step and returns the batch ID with a result per item; `files.batchRename.undo(result)` undoes that batch.
Regular expressions behave exactly like `RegExp` in scripts, and `RegExp` objects can be passed directly. `planAsync`, `applyAsync` and `undoAsync` return promises.

faq.q: Why is there no launcher icon?
faq.a: The plugin has no standalone entry. AutoJs6 discovers it after installation, and everything happens in the AutoJs6 file manager or in scripts.

faq.q: Does the plugin need storage permission?
faq.a: No. The plugin only computes new names from file names; AutoJs6 lists folders and renames files with the access it already has.

faq.q: How does it differ from PowerRename?
faq.a: Date variables use the modification time, because creation times are unreliable on Android. It adds Unicode normalization, full-width conversion, illegal character cleanup and undoable batch records. Photo EXIF variables are planned for 1.1.0.

p_security_intro: The plugin keeps its permission surface small:
security_points: Least privilege: the Manifest only declares the AutoJs6 plugin permission (`org.autojs.permission.PLUGIN`), with no network or storage permission.
Host execution: the plugin only returns a rename plan; AutoJs6 validates every item again before renaming and never overwrites existing files unless the overwrite policy is chosen explicitly.
Protected entry points: the services and the rename screen require the plugin permission, so other apps cannot call them.
